text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended on Thursday.

LONDON - British shares closed higher, inspired by Wall Street's continuing advance, the return of domestic bid speculation and positive results from one of Britain's top companies. The FTSE 100 index finished up 22.8 points at 4,327.1.

FRANKFURT - The German DAX index ended bourse trade on another record closing high, continuing its record run of recent weeks inspired by the cast-iron resilience of the dollar at 1.68 marks, the firmness of DTB futures and the 1.51 percent-higher close on Wall Street overnight. The DAX-30 index closed at 3,229.48 up 13.34 points. In post-bourse trade the DAX index stood at 3,256.86.

PARIS - French shares closed at a fresh record high after a 1.2 percent jump, underpinned by a rising dollar and further gains on Wall Street, the market shrugged off January U.S. retail sales, which were broadly in line with expectations, and lower weekly jobless claims. The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed up 29.08 points or 1.12 percent at 2,628.41.

ZURICH - The Swiss bourse's ten-day run of record closings ended on Thursday as profit taking pulled shares down from an early all-time high of 4,467.4 points on the Swiss Market Index (SMI). Dealers welcomed the correction, saying it was not expected to dampen overall favourable sentiment. One trader added that buying regularly sets in once prices start to slip.
The all-share Swiss Performance Index (SPI) ended down 1.95 points to 2,824.34 points.

TOKYO - Tokyo stocks rallied for the third consecutive day, inspired by the weak yen which supported blue-chip buying and Nippon Credit Bank Ltds recovery, Wall Streets record climb was also a supportive factor for the market. The Nikkei average of leading 225 issues finished up 278.10 points at 18,688.06.

HONG KONG - Hong Kong stocks tumbled to a sharply lower close, as stock index futures plummeted and worries remerged about the health of China's paramount leader Deng Xiaoping. The Hang Seng Index slid 222.66 points or 1.65 percent to 13,239.95.

SYDNEY - A confident Australian share market smashed records to close higher with traders in an upbeat mood as big banks and miners showed the way up. The All Ordinaries index jumped 22.9 points to 2,496.4.

JOHANNESBURG - South African shares rose in hectic trade to close strong in record volumes, Industrials were firm riding on the back of firm Wall Street and golds leapt on a $6 recovery in the bullion price, sentiment was positive boosted by the steady rand and a bouyant bonds market, with Finance Minister Trevor Manuel's comments bullish for the market. The All-share index ended up 70 points at 6,966, Industrials gained 70 points to 8,263 and the Gold index made 40 points to 1,350.
